Mario Draghi, the 'sphinx' still shaping the EU's agenda
subhead: At 79, the former president of the European Central Bank, who no longer holds any official office, remains at the heart of European Union politics. Elusive and deliberately secretive, he skillfully leverages his ability to speak to political leaders, business executives, and financial markets alike.

title: 'Public opinion is ahead of the media discourse on AI'
subhead: While media coverage of artificial intelligence (AI) often swings between enthusiastic techno-optimism and dire warnings, Western public opinion has taken a strikingly pragmatic view on how to approach the technology, writes sociologist Tibor Dessewffy.

title: French Football Federation withdraws support for embattled FIFA President Infantino
subhead: During a meeting of its executive committee on Thursday, the FFF formally ended ties with the head of world football's governing body, who has faced widespread criticism following his failed commercial partnership project and is seeking re-election in March 2027.

title: Theft of two Renoir paintings in southern France reignites debate over vulnerability of cultural sites
subhead: Stolen from the Musée Renoir in Cagnes-sur-Mer on Tuesday, the paintings add to a growing list of artworks taken in recent months, a trend that prompted the French minister of culture to announce an emergency action plan in July.

Fifty years after Mao's death, China still grapples with his legacy
subhead: 'Mao's Fraught Legacy' (1/7). Mao Zedong, who died on September 9, 1976, founded the People's Republic of China and still casts a shadow over the country's political life. The Chinese Communist Party, whose power base Mao established, remains divided between loyalty to his myth and condemnation of his 'mistakes,' which led to the deaths of tens of millions of people.

title: Why loneliness is now seen as a harmful epidemic for mental and physical health
subhead: In France, nearly one in four people reported feeling lonely in 2025. This isolation particularly affects young people and the elderly, and could be a significant source of suffering. Among the possible ways to counter it are taking part in local activities and encouraging more volunteering.
